{{Short description|Mathematical term}}
{{No footnotes|date=July 2025}}
In [[mathematics]], a '''slender group''' is a [[torsion-free group|torsion-free]] [[abelian group]] that is "small" in a sense that is made precise in the definition below.

== Definition ==

Let <math>\mathbb Z^{\mathbb{N}}</math> denote the [[Baer–Specker group]], that is, the [[group (mathematics)|group]] of all [[integer sequence]]s, with termwise addition. For each [[natural number]] <math>n</math>, let <math>e_n</math> be the sequence with <math>n</math>-th term equal to 1 and all other terms 0.

A torsion-free abelian group <math>G</math> is said to be '''slender''' if every [[group homomorphism|homomorphism]] from <math>\mathbb Z^{\mathbb{N}}</math> into <math>G</math> maps all but finitely many of the <math>e_n</math> to the [[identity element]].

== Examples ==

Every [[free abelian group]] is slender.

The additive group of [[rational number]]s <math>\mathbb Q</math> is not slender: any mapping of the <math>e_n</math> into <math>\mathbb Q</math> extends to a homomorphism from the free [[subgroup]] generated by the <math>e_n</math>, and as <math>\mathbb Q</math> is [[injective module|injective]] this homomorphism extends over the whole of <math>\mathbb Z^{\mathbb{N}}</math>. Therefore, a slender group must be [[reduced abelian group|reduced]].

Every [[countable set|countable]] reduced torsion-free abelian group is slender, so every proper subgroup of <math>\mathbb Q</math> is slender.

== Properties ==
* A torsion-free abelian group is slender [[if and only if]] it is reduced and contains no copy of the Baer–Specker group and no copy of the [[p-adic integers|<math>p</math>-adic integers]] for any <math>p</math>.
* Direct sums of slender groups are also slender.
* Subgroups of slender groups are slender.
* Every homomorphism from <math>\mathbb Z^{\mathbb{N}}</math> into a slender group factors through <math>\mathbb Z^n</math> for some natural number <math>n</math>.
